introduction: A namespace is an organizational boundary, not an automatic firewall. This lesson separates three questions: what the application process can do, what its Kubernetes identity can request, and which network connections it can make.

Replace the disposable kind cluster with one using Cilium so packet-policy tests have an enforcing implementation. This is an explicit add-on operating obligation: version, privileges, compatibility and removal must be understood. A NetworkPolicy object alone proves no packets were blocked.
prerequisites: Ubuntu 24.04 Bash in WSL2 or a disposable Linux VM; Docker is running. Use the same terminal unless a step names a second terminal.
Weeks25–26 manifests and local devopps-taskboard:w25 image. Keep lab evidence before removing the old cluster. This lesson uses a single-node Cilium cluster; no resilience claim.

concepts.title: Different identities, different controls
paragraphs: runAsNonRoot and capability removal constrain the process inside the container. A ServiceAccount identifies a workload to the Kubernetes API. RBAC grants verbs on resources. These do not grant or deny SQL access.

Secrets are API objects; their base64 representation is reversible. Anyone authorized to read the Secret can recover its value. Limit RBAC, protect etcd backups and use encryption-at-rest/external secret delivery in a production design.
concepts.example: A process can be non-root yet read every Secret if its API identity has that permission.
concepts.judgment: Do not mount a service-account token when the app never calls the API. A dashboard such as Headlamp should use the same least-privilege reasoning.

concepts.title: Policies are additive selection rules
paragraphs: A policy selects source or destination Pods. Once selected for a direction, only traffic allowed by the union of applicable policies is permitted. DNS is a separate dependency; allow UDP and TCP53 to the real cluster DNS Pods.
The lab tests TCP reachability to PostgreSQL independently of SQL authentication. A successful TCP connection says the route is available, not that a query is authorized.
concepts.example: An allowed app connects to5432 while an unlabeled diagnostic Pod times out.
concepts.judgment: A policy that allows every namespace defeats an intended same-namespace restriction. Inspect selectors and prove both allowed and denied paths.

steps.title: Install an enforcing network layer
steps.purpose: Rebuild only the named disposable cluster, then restore known desired state.

commands.code:
export KUBECONFIG="$HOME/dev-opps-lab/k8s/kubeconfig"
kubectl config current-context
cd "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/k8s"
kind delete cluster --name devopps
cat > kind-policy.yaml <<'YAML'
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
- role: control-plane
networking:
  disableDefaultCNI: true
YAML
kind create cluster --name devopps-policy --config kind-policy.yaml --kubeconfig "$KUBECONFIG"
CLI_VERSION=$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cilium/cilium-cli/main/stable.txt)
case "$(uname -m)" in x86_64) ARCH=amd64 ;; aarch64) ARCH=arm64 ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
curl -fLO "https://github.com/cilium/cilium-cli/releases/download/$CLI_VERSION/cilium-linux-$ARCH.tar.gz"
curl -fLO "https://github.com/cilium/cilium-cli/releases/download/$CLI_VERSION/cilium-linux-$ARCH.tar.gz.sha256sum"
sha256sum --check "cilium-linux-$ARCH.tar.gz.sha256sum"
tar -xzf "cilium-linux-$ARCH.tar.gz" -C "$HOME/.local/bin" cilium
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
cilium install --version 1.20.3 --set ipam.mode=kubernetes --set operator.replicas=1
cilium status --wait
kind load docker-image devopps-taskboard:w25 --name devopps-policy
kubectl create namespace devopps
kubectl apply -f app-probed.yaml -f service.yaml
explain: delete cluster targets only the previous lab; its in-memory data was disposable. disableDefaultCNI leaves node networking unready until Cilium is installed.

Resolve the official CLI release once, download its architecture-specific archive and checksum, then verify before extracting only cilium into the user bin directory. -xzf extracts gzip; -C selects the destination.

cilium install pins the network component release; ipam.mode=kubernetes uses Kubernetes-assigned Pod ranges. One operator replica is an explicit local resource compromise. status --wait checks installation before loading/applying workloads.
commands.expected: Context kind-devopps-policy; Cilium ready and Taskboard returns to2/2.
commands.troubleshoot: If the checksum fails stop. If nodes remain NotReady inspect cilium status and kube-system events; do not proceed to policy claims until CNI health is established.

steps.checkpoint: Record Cilium version and why privileged networking software is needed on cluster nodes.

steps.title: Constrain process and API identity
steps.purpose: Give the application no mounted API credential and demonstrate a narrow observer identity.

commands.code:
kubectl -n devopps create serviceaccount taskboard
kubectl -n devopps create serviceaccount observer
kubectl -n devopps create role pod-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods
kubectl -n devopps create rolebinding observer-read --role=pod-reader --serviceaccount=devopps:observer
kubectl auth can-i list pods -n devopps --as=system:serviceaccount:devopps:observer
kubectl auth can-i get secrets -n devopps --as=system:serviceaccount:devopps:observer
cat > hardening.json <<'JSON'
{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"serviceAccountName":"taskboard","automountServiceAccountToken":false,"securityContext":{"runAsNonRoot":true,"runAsUser":10001,"seccompProfile":{"type":"RuntimeDefault"}},"containers":[{"name":"app","securityContext":{"allowPrivilegeEscalation":false,"readOnlyRootFilesystem":true,"capabilities":{"drop":["ALL"]}}}]}}}}
JSON
kubectl patch --local -f app-probed.yaml --type=strategic --patch-file hardening.json -o yaml > app-secure.yaml
kubectl apply -f app-secure.yaml
kubectl -n devopps rollout status deployment/taskboard --timeout=180s
explain: The Role grants only Pod reads inside devopps. RoleBinding associates it with observer. can-i --as asks the authorization system about that identity; this administrator-driven test is not a token login.

The patch selects the dedicated app account and disables token mounting. UID10001 matches the image. RuntimeDefault seccomp, no privilege escalation, read-only root and drop ALL reduce available process operations. Save the complete result in app-secure.yaml.
commands.expected: Observer list pods=yes and get secrets=no; app remains Ready.
commands.troubleshoot: An unexpected yes indicates an additional binding; permissions are additive. If a read-only filesystem breaks startup, identify the exact required writable path rather than disabling the protection globally.

steps.checkpoint: Explain why a non-root UID and least-privilege RBAC are independent controls.

steps.title: Prove database reachability boundaries
steps.purpose: Use a disposable PostgreSQL listener and positive/negative clients.

commands.code:
kubectl -n devopps create secret generic pg-lab --from-literal=password="$(python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(24))')"
cat > pg-network.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: postgres, namespace: devopps}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: postgres}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: postgres}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:17
        env:
        - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
          valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-lab, key: password}}
        ports: [{containerPort: 5432}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: postgres, namespace: devopps}
spec:
  selector: {app: postgres}
  ports: [{port: 5432, targetPort: 5432}]
YAML
kubectl apply -f pg-network.yaml
kubectl -n devopps rollout status deployment/postgres --timeout=180s
cat > boundary.yaml <<'YAML'
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: database-boundary, namespace: devopps}
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app: postgres}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels: {app: taskboard}
    ports:
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 5432}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: app-egress, namespace: devopps}
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app: taskboard}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels: {app: postgres}
    ports:
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 5432}
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system}
      podSelector:
        matchLabels: {k8s-app: kube-dns}
    ports:
    - {protocol: UDP, port: 53}
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 53}
YAML
kubectl apply -f boundary.yaml
kubectl -n devopps exec deployment/taskboard -- python -c 'import socket; socket.create_connection(("postgres",5432),3).close(); print("TCP_ALLOWED")'
kubectl -n devopps run outsider --image=busybox:1.37 --restart=Never --command -- sleep 3600
kubectl -n devopps wait --for=condition=Ready pod/outsider --timeout=120s
kubectl -n devopps exec outsider -- nc -z -w 3 postgres 5432
explain: Python secrets produces a random lab password; create secret passes it into an API Secret rather than storing it in a manifest. Do not copy Secret YAML into Git. PostgreSQL has no persistent volume in this transport-only drill.
The heredocs provide the entire Deployment, Service and policies. Database ingress selects only taskboard Pods in this namespace. App egress allows database TCP5432 and DNS53 to kube-system/kube-dns.

Python create_connection checks the allowed path with a3-second timeout. The outsider has no matching app label. nc -z checks without sending SQL; -w3 bounds the denied connection attempt. A nonzero exit is expected.
commands.expected: Taskboard prints TCP_ALLOWED; outsider times out/nonzero.
commands.troubleshoot: If both clients connect, the CNI or policy selection is wrong. If neither connects, verify PostgreSQL logs/readiness, then DNS and selectors. Do not treat denial of both as success.

steps.checkpoint: Record both results; label them transport evidence, not SQL authorization evidence.

failure.title: App egress omitted DNS
failure.boundary: Only the app-egress policy in the isolated namespace.

explain: JSON Patch removes the DNS rule by index while keeping database egress.
inject.expected: New hostname resolution from the app fails.
inject.troubleshoot: Resolve in a fresh process to avoid cached DNS.

investigate.code:
kubectl -n devopps exec deployment/taskboard -- python -c 'import socket; print(socket.getaddrinfo("postgres",5432))'
kubectl -n devopps get networkpolicy app-egress -o yaml
explain: The first command isolates DNS; the second shows the missing permitted destination.
investigate.expected: Resolution fails while the database rule remains.
investigate.troubleshoot: Inspect actual DNS Pod labels if a restored rule still does not work.

hints: Does database IP access differ from hostname access?
Which protocol is needed before TCP5432?

explanation: The app was allowed to contact the database but could no longer discover its IP. Restore the narrowly scoped DNS rule; allowing all egress would hide the cause.

verification.code: kubectl -n devopps exec deployment/taskboard -- python -c 'import socket; socket.create_connection(("postgres",5432),3).close(); print("RECOVERED")'
explain: Retest name resolution plus TCP connection.
verification.troubleshoot: Repeat the outsider test to ensure recovery did not broaden access.

questions.answer: It transports bytes safely in text; it supplies no confidentiality. Access control and encryption address different threats.

questions.hint: What if there is no enforcing CNI?
questions.answer: An allow test succeeds on an open network too. Denial proves the selected boundary affects real packets.
No Role rule grants it. Verify with kubectl auth can-i patch deployments -n devopps --as=system:serviceaccount:devopps:observer.

exercise.brief: Create an observer permission table and a three-edge network diagram.
hints: Inspect bindings as well as the Role.
solution: List every granted verb/resource; test a secret read and a Deployment patch are denied. Draw DNS as its own dependency and attach command output to each network edge.

cleanup.code:
kubectl -n devopps delete pod outsider
kubectl -n devopps delete -f "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/k8s/pg-network.yaml"
kubectl -n devopps delete secret pg-lab
kubectl -n devopps delete networkpolicy database-boundary app-egress
explain: Remove the transport-only database, random credential and drill policies; retain hardened Taskboard and the enforcing cluster. Policies are restored explicitly in later database exercises.
cleanup.expected: Temporary objects deleted; app stays available.
cleanup.troubleshoot: The database contained no meaningful data. Never reuse this deletion procedure for a persistent production database.

repoConnections.application: Record why the network plugin is necessary, how it fails, the version used and the cluster-removal route.

repoConnections.principle: A dashboard is an API client.
repoConnections.application: The observer Role is a concrete limited troubleshooting identity; a GUI must not quietly broaden it.

title: Configuration and workload security
outcome: Limit workload permissions and verify network isolation.
